transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-21
Time: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Li (CEO), Diego Ramos (CTO), Priya Sharma (VP Product), Eli Turner (Head Eng), Jordan Reed (Head People), Sam Brooks (CFO) + all-employees stream

[00:00] Maya Li: ok uh good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining today's all hands, sorry we're a bit overbooked on the west coast times so appreciate flexibility. I'm Maya, we'll kick off with a short strategy update then dive into people stuff — the careers sprint — and finish with product and Q&A.

[00:26] Diego Ramos: quick note — audio's a little low for some attendees, if you can't hear pls ping express chat.

[00:40] Maya Li: first slide, high level, we've been tracking product-led growth and the metrics are generally positive, usage up 28% q/q, latency p50 is steady but p95 still has pockets. main message: prioritize reliability and predictable economics for customers this quarter. that means targeted infra investments and focused hiring.

[01:15] Priya Sharma: on product, milestones for the next 90 days — 1) release the batching cache improvements, 2) deliver the model routing UI in Console, 3) finalize the Optimize suggestions flow. We know customers want clearer recommendations for quantization and batching; that's a big one.

[01:48] Eli Turner: from eng ops, we're rolling out extra tracing hooks and a canary for the new KV-cache behavior. initial perf tests look promising but we still see tail latency with long-context chat sessions. we're creating a dedicated runbook for those scenarios.

[02:18] Maya Li: thanks Eli. quick business context: sales is seeing enterprise deals that are more security-driven — private deployments and VPC is a clear ask — so our product + infra work needs to back that. Sam, brief on budget?

[02:38] Sam Brooks: sure. short version: hiring is still a priority but H2 needs tighter guardrails. we plan to keep critical roles (infra, reliability, senior infra engs) open, but we'll cap net hires in non-critical teams unless there's a clear ROI. the CFO team will publish a hiring rubric next week.

[03:05] Jordan Reed: people update — we're launching a two-week "careers sprint" starting next monday. objectives: (a) make promotions predictable, (b) accelerate role clarity and career ladders, (c) run compensation calibration. we'll do manager training, cross-checks, and open office hours. it's intense but necessary.

[03:35] Maya Li: want to emphasize this — careers sprint is not a surprise layoff exercise. it's about clarity and fairness, making growth pathways visible. we know that ambiguity drives churn.

[03:56] Attendee (Q): uh why are we doing this so suddenly, feels rushed?

[04:04] Jordan Reed: good question. last quarter's signals — retention dips on mid-senior ICs — and we have to move faster to set expectations. also aligning comp cycles and promotions so people feel seen.

[04:26] Priya Sharma: from product side we'll publish role expectations for product managers and PM-IC ladders during the sprint.

[04:40] Diego Ramos: engineering will publish competency matrices for infra and runtime teams. they won't be perfect, but they're better than the current ad-hoc docs.

[05:02] Maya Li: okay roadmap + operational focus — we think customers will judge us on two things: consistent latency/p95 and predictable cost per token. Optimize and Dedicated both play into that.

[05:22] Eli Turner: operationally, small belt-tightening: limit major infra migrations during careers sprint window to avoid noisy experiments. we'll communicate windows.

[05:40] Maya Li: moving to hiring and compensation — Sam, what's the immediate impact for offers?

[05:46] Sam Brooks: offers are still going out for critical hires but comp packages will be calibrated. if managers need exceptions we ask for business case and senior leadership sign-off.

[06:05] Maya Li: ok, a few quick signals on product: Priya, can you outline the milestone timeline?

[06:12] Priya Sharma: yes — by end of April: batching cache PRs merged to staging; early May: model routing UI beta; mid-May: Optimize suggestions in alpha to internal customers. dependent on a few infra optimizations and SRE support.

[06:40] Attendee (Slack question read): will this affect the internal hiring freeze that some folks are hearing about?

[06:48] Jordan Reed: the freeze is not company-wide — it's constrained to non-essential hires. teams with clear SLIs and growth potential can apply for exceptions.

[07:05] Maya Li: thanks. now a short section on risk and competitive landscape — Diego?

[07:12] Diego Ramos: BigCloudAI launched aggressive pricing last quarter and ModelServeCo is pushing private endpoints with simplified procurement. our angle is performance plus operational experience; we need to double down on observability and SLO-driven SLAs.

[07:36] Maya Li: we will not chase a pure price war. instead emphasize product differentiation: unified runtime, predictable economics, and better support for private deployments.

[07:50] Priya Sharma: also, we will highlight evaluation artifacts — benchmark sheets + short videos — in our sales kit. ccs: rev ops and marketing to sync.

[08:05] Maya Li: ok, open Q&A. reminder: we have limited time, we'll prioritize questions submitted in chat.

[08:15] Attendee (Anon): can you talk to the promotion cadence for senior ICs?

[08:22] Jordan Reed: promotion criteria: impact, craft, leadership. during the sprint we'll do manager calibrations and some live calibration sessions. expect clearer timelines.

[08:36] Attendee (Eng): how will infra hiring be prioritized across regions?

[08:44] Eli Turner: prioritization will be based on latency/regional demand and pool availability. for immediate needs we'll hire in the region with the strongest candidate pipeline, otherwise remote-first.

[09:05] Attendee (Product): what's the measurable success for the careers sprint?

[09:11] Priya Sharma: success metrics: reduced time-to-promotion (target -30% median), lowered voluntary attrition for targeted cohorts, and percent of role descriptions published (target 90%).

[09:36] Maya Li: quick note on incidents — we had two incidents that impacted latency in March; postmortems are in process. Eli?

[09:44] Eli Turner: main cause was a combination of batching config regression and a misrouted fallback. we've got fixes in code-review and a new alerting rule. we'll share the postmortem doc later today.

[10:05] Maya Li: good. now we want to close with concrete next steps and timing. Jordan will post the careers sprint calendar + office hours. Priya will publish the product milestone doc. Sam will circulate headcount constraints. Diego and Eli will post the reliability runbook links.

[10:25] Maya Li: again want to say — this is about clarity and fairness. we'll iterate and be open with the outcomes. appreciate everyone's focus.

[10:36] Attendee (HR question): will compensation changes be retroactive?

[10:41] Jordan Reed: no broad retroactive increases are planned. there will be adjustments as part of calibration but most changes are effective at the next comp cycle unless exceptions are approved.

[11:00] Attendee (Sales): for enterprise deals asking for on-prem, do we have a clear template?

[11:07] Priya Sharma: yes, there's a partner pack and a private deployment checklist, but we plan to make it more customer-facing. Rev ops will update the kit.

[11:28] Maya Li: thanks. final quick pulse — two poll questions in chat: do you feel directions are clearer? and do you feel supported in career growth? we'll leave the poll open for 24 hours.

[11:40] Maya Li: wrap — TL;DR: focus on reliability, careers sprint next two weeks, targeted hires only, product milestones with clear owner deadlines. expect the follow-ups in Slack and email.

[11:55] Diego Ramos: thanks all.

[12:00] End of recording.
